3.modern-en: Negotiates the loan of three thousand ducats with Bassanio. When Antonio arrives, Shylock recounts years of insult — being called a dog, being spat upon — and proposes the pound-of-flesh bond, framing it as a 'merry sport.'

8.modern-en: Orders Jessica to lock up the house during the Christian masque. Uneasy about the festivities, he warns her against the sound of music and shallow foppery.

13.modern-en: Learns that Jessica has fled with Lorenzo and his money. Delivers the 'Hath not a Jew eyes?' speech, arguing that if Christians wrong a Jew, a Jew will seek revenge — just as Christians taught him. Hears that Antonio's ships have been lost and resolves to enforce the bond.

15.modern-en: Encounters Antonio in custody and refuses all pleas for mercy. Insists he will have his bond. His determination is absolute.

18.modern-en: In court, refuses the Duke's plea for mercy and Bassanio's offer of double payment. Portia, disguised as a lawyer, first urges mercy, then finds a legal technicality: the bond allows flesh but not blood. Shylock is found guilty of conspiring against a citizen's life. He is forced to convert to Christianity, surrender half his wealth to Antonio and half to the state, and name Lorenzo and Jessica as his heirs. He leaves the court broken.

2.modern-en: Introduced with Nerissa at Belmont, weary of the casket test her dead father imposed. Reviews her suitors with sharp, witty dismissals of each. Remembers Bassanio fondly.

10.modern-en: Watches the Prince of Morocco choose the gold casket. He finds a death's head inside and departs. Portia remarks she hopes all suitors of his complexion choose likewise.

14.modern-en: Urges Bassanio to wait before choosing, afraid of losing him. He chooses the lead casket and wins her. She gives him a ring and makes him swear never to part with it. The celebration is interrupted by news of Antonio's peril.

16.modern-en: Devises her plan to save Antonio. Sends to her cousin Doctor Bellario for legal robes and disguises herself as a young lawyer named Balthazar. Leaves Belmont for Venice.

18.modern-en: Arrives at the trial disguised as Balthazar. Delivers the 'quality of mercy' speech. When Shylock refuses mercy, she turns the law against him: the bond specifies flesh but not blood, and as an alien who conspired against a citizen's life, Shylock's property and life are forfeit. After the verdict, she tricks Bassanio into giving up the ring she gave him.

20.modern-en: Returns to Belmont ahead of Bassanio. Confronts him about the missing ring, pretending outrage, before revealing she was the lawyer who saved Antonio. All is reconciled. She delivers news that Antonio's ships have come home safely after all.

1.modern-en: Opens the play with an unexplained melancholy. His friends suggest his sadness stems from worry over his ships at sea or from being in love; he denies both. Agrees to help Bassanio court Portia.

3.modern-en: Accompanies Bassanio to Shylock. Despite his history of insulting Shylock, he agrees to the pound-of-flesh bond, confident his ships will return well before the deadline.

15.modern-en: In the custody of a jailer, he begs Shylock to hear him out but is refused. Accepts that Shylock will have his bond and asks only that Bassanio come to watch him pay it.

18.modern-en: In court, prepares calmly for death. After Portia's legal maneuver saves him, he is given half of Shylock's wealth (which he will hold in trust for Lorenzo and Jessica). Persuades Bassanio to give up the ring to the disguised Portia.

1.modern-en: Confides in Antonio that he has found a way to clear his debts: by courting the wealthy Portia in Belmont. He needs money for the venture and asks Antonio for help.

3.modern-en: Negotiates with Shylock for the three-thousand-ducat loan. Is uneasy about the pound-of-flesh condition but Antonio overrides his concern.

14.modern-en: Arrives at Belmont and faces the casket test. Chooses the lead casket — 'Who chooseth me must give and hazard all he hath' — and finds Portia's portrait inside. Wins her hand. Receives Portia's ring with the condition that he must never part with it.

18.modern-en: In court, offers Shylock double and triple the debt to release Antonio. After the verdict, the disguised Portia asks for his ring as payment. He refuses at first, then gives it up at Antonio's urging.

20.modern-en: Returns to Belmont and is confronted by Portia about the missing ring. Swears he gave it to the lawyer who saved Antonio. Portia reveals the truth and forgives him.

6.modern-en: Says goodbye to Launcelot and confesses that her father's house is hell to her. Gives Lorenzo a letter and plans her elopement, ashamed of disguising herself as a boy.

9.modern-en: Escapes from Shylock's house during the masque, disguised as a torchbearer. Throws down a casket of gold and jewels to Lorenzo. They flee Venice together.

17.modern-en: At Belmont with Lorenzo, she is teased by Launcelot about her father's sins. Defends her conversion to Christianity through her marriage.

20.modern-en: Opens Act V with Lorenzo in a moonlit exchange of romantic classical allusions at Belmont. Learns she and Lorenzo will inherit Shylock's wealth.
